title: How Stonehenge Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore Stonehenge in Wiltshire, England: its earthwork ditch-and-bank construction (a reverse henge), the origin and transport of the sarsen and bluestones, the trilithons and lintels with mortise-and-tenon style carving, the Aubrey holes and earlier timber post holes, the Avenue aligned with solstice sunrise and sunset, Durrington Walls across the River Avon, debunked theories (Druids, giants, Merlin, glacial movement, King James I excavation), modern theories (burial ground for elites, unification monument, acoustics), and the 1985 Battle of the Beanfield with New Age Travellers. Episode closes with listener mail about tuna and onion flavored gelato.

segments.title: Opening banter and travel
segments.summary: Josh returns from New Zealand and Okinawa and talks about the trip; the hosts tease a future live show and set up the Stonehenge topic.

segments.title: What a henge is and Stonehenge's reverse henge design
segments.summary: A henge is an earthwork of a bank and ditch; Stonehenge is a reverse henge with the ditch outside the bank. Crop circles are noted as originating in the same area. Dating places the construction over a period of under two hundred years, and the site is eight miles north of Salisbury.

segments.title: Druid myth and the age of Stonehenge
segments.summary: Nineteenth-century antiquarians linked Stonehenge to the Druids, but the Druids postdate the monument; the earthworks date back at least five thousand years and the large stones to roughly 2500-2000 BCE, around the time of the Great Pyramids.

segments.title: Transporting the megaliths
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the massive stones were moved without the wheel, including the glacial theory that was discarded, rollers and stone ball bearings, and stone weights ranging from about two to five tons.

segments.title: Sarsen stones, lintels, trilithons and bluestones
segments.summary: Describes the upright sarsen stones sourced from the Marlborough Downs about twenty miles away, the lintels on top, the carved joinery in the trilithons, the roughly thirty-foot inner trilithons, the outer ring, and the named stones and bluestones of differing rock types.

segments.title: Merlin legend, solstice Avenue and the Aubrey holes
segments.summary: The Merlin and Irish-giant legend is recounted; the Avenue aligned with solstice sun is discussed; the hinge is dug with deer antler picks; the Aubrey holes and earlier timber post holes found during 1960s parking-lot excavation are described, along with the later bluestone phase and Blue Stone Henge near the River Avon.

segments.title: Durrington Walls, burials and theories of purpose
segments.summary: Durrington Walls across the River Avon is described as a possible builders' camp and settlement; cremated remains suggest a burial ground for elites; the Amesbury Archer and healing theories, King James I's excavation, and modern theories such as unification and a power display are covered.

segments.title: Acoustics and the Battle of the Beanfield
segments.summary: Acoustic theories and the piper legend are mentioned. The hosts recount the 1985 Battle of the Beanfield between police and New Age Travellers, the later reopening of the site for the solstice by English Heritage in 2000, and the modern solstice gathering.

segments.title: Listener mail: tuna and onion gelato
segments.summary: Nathan writes about tuna gelato in Atlanta and an onion gelato he tried in Tropea, Italy. Hosts thank High Road Creamery for ice cream.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give contact info and sign off.
